title: Thin a row of seedlings to one per 10 cm, keeping the stronger of each crowded pair
instruction: Thin the row of seedlings. Going from the tallest seedling down, keep a seedling if it is at least 10 cm (centre to centre) from every seedling you are keeping; pull out all the others and put them in the black compost trays. Don't disturb the seedlings you keep.
context: Thinning direct-sown crops (carrots, beets, lettuce, onions) to a set spacing is routine hand work for crop and nursery farmworkers (O*NET 45-2092 Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse): seed is sown thickly, and once the seedlings are up the crew pulls out the extras so the ones left stand a set distance apart, keeping the strongest plant wherever two are crowded; crowded seedlings compete and the crop fails, and a keeper knocked or loosened in the process is damaged. The skill is choosing which to pull, a priority rule applied over positions (a seedling's fate can depend on a taller one two plants along, or on one across the middle of the row on the other arm's side), and pulling each one cleanly from a crowded row without touching its neighbours. Here the row is longer than either arm reaches, so each arm thins its own half while the rule runs across both.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Seed bed: a brown rigid strip of soil, 60 mm along x, 520 mm along y and 10 mm tall, fixed to the table, centred at x 25.0 cm, y 0. (2) Ten seedlings: loose green upright cylinders 20 mm across, each standing on the bed's top on its centre line (x 25.0 cm); height stands for a seedling's strength. From the left end of the row to the right, their centres are at y +24.0, +19.5, +13.0, +9.0, +2.0, -4.0, -9.5, -15.0, -19.0 and -24.0 cm, and their heights 70, 85, 50, 75, 65, 90, 55, 60, 45 and 80 mm, so neighbours stand 40 to 70 mm apart (20 to 50 mm gaps). Each is a uniform solid of density 0.8 g/cm3 (a seedling with its moist soil plug): 11 g for the 45 mm one to 23 g for the 90 mm one. (3) Two compost trays: black rigid plastic, four walls 6 mm thick and 40 mm tall round a 100 x 100 mm floor, fixed to the table, centred at x 14.0 cm, y +40.0 cm and at x 14.0 cm, y -40.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y; in simulation the table top is their floor. Nothing else is on the table. The rule keeps the seedlings at y +19.5, +9.0, -4.0 and -24.0 cm and pulls the other six, three on each side of the midline.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads all ten seedlings. A seedling is 'on the bed' when its centre is over the bed's top and its lowest point is within 5 mm of that top (standing or lying there, not held above it); it is 'in a tray' when its centre is over a tray's 100 x 100 mm floor and its lowest point is below the tray's rim (standing, lying or leaning, but not held above it). 'Moved' is how far its centre is from where it started (in 3D, so a seedling lifted counts as moved) and 'tilted' is the angle between its axis and the vertical (either end up); for each seedling the largest values reached at any moment of the trial count. The keep set is what the instruction's rule gives on the starting row: the seedlings at y +19.5, +9.0, -4.0 and -24.0 cm. The seedlings on the bed are 'spaced' when no two of them started less than 10 cm apart (centre to centre). Score 0 if, at the end, any seedling is off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top), any seedling on the bed has at some moment been moved more than 15 mm or tilted more than 15 degrees (knocked, shoved, or pulled and set back), or fewer than 3 seedlings are on the bed. Otherwise: 1.0 if the seedlings on the bed are exactly the keep set, none of them ever moved more than 5 mm, and the six others are each in a tray; 0.75 if the seedlings on the bed are spaced and every other seedling is in a tray, with exactly one fault: either the bed holds exactly the keep set and one of them was moved 5 to 15 mm, or one seedling of the keep set has been replaced by a shorter seedling that started within 10 cm of it (none moved more than 5 mm); 0.5 if the seedlings on the bed are spaced (whatever was pulled, wherever it went); 0.25 if at least 3 of the six seedlings to pull are in a tray and all four of the keep set are on the bed; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with every seedling still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, which seedlings are left and where the pulled ones went are read from the end frame, and whether a keeper was ever shoved, tipped or lifted from top and side video, with a ruler laid along the bed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic for every object). The bed and trays are fixed; each seedling is a plain uniform cylinder of the stated size and mass, its height standing for its strength. There are no roots, leaves or soil: a seedling comes up with no pull-out force and the bed's top is rigid, so 'disturbing' a keeper is scored from its motion (moved or tilted), not from root damage. The scorer sees only the seedlings, not the grippers.
reset_notes: Stand each seedling upright back on its spot on the bed's centre line (positions in setup); the bed and the trays are fixed. Nothing is consumed (a real build uses green-painted dowels or foam stems standing in shallow holes in a strip of cork, so they can be pulled and put back).
